title: The Harvest of the Undercroft
premise: Felix Halloran is sent to appraise Undercroft House, a derelict farmhouse whose measurements refuse to stay constant, and finds his childhood imaginary friend, Wick, waiting on the porch exactly as he left him thirty years ago. Wick reveals the house's founders bound themselves into its walls through a harvest ritual that demands a returning 'keeper' every generation — and Felix was chosen as a child, then smuggled away before the binding could complete. To survive the house's hunger and free the souls already harvested, Felix must finish the ritual the founders abandoned, sacrificing his own memories of belonging as the price. He completes it at terrible cost: the house releases its dead and crumbles, but Felix walks out unable to remember his own name, carrying only Wick's hand in his.
about_author: Ines Dunmore is the pen name of a former land registry clerk from rural Ohio who spent a decade cataloguing houses that no one would buy twice. Her fiction draws on county archives, abandoned homesteads, and the conviction that property remembers its owners.

chapters.title: The Appraisal
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. A burned-out surveyor arrives at Undercroft House to appraise it for a bank, noting wrong details: doors that outnumber the blueprint's count, rooms warmer than the weather allows. He keeps his professional checklist like a talisman. Emotional beat: brittle control masking loneliness, established through his ritual of counting and lighting lamps.

chapters.title: Wick on the Porch
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. At dusk he finds a small figure on the porch — Wick, his childhood imaginary friend, unchanged, who greets him by a nickname no living person knows. Felix's rationality wars with recognition. Emotional beat: terror braided with a shameful flood of homecoming; the first crack in his armor.

chapters.title: Measurements That Move
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Overnight the house's dimensions shift; his laser measurements differ by feet between readings, and a hallway appears that wasn't there. Wick warns him not to map the third floor. Emotional beat: professional competence curdling into helplessness as the house 'appraises him back.'

chapters.title: The Founders' Ledger
chapters.summary: Felix's POV, with ledger excerpts. In the cellar he finds the Undercroft founders' ledger — a harvest record of names, dates, and 'yields' spanning 150 years, the final entry his own childhood name, marked 'deferred.' Emotional beat: dread of discovering he was always expected.

chapters.title: What the House Remembers
chapters.summary: Wick's POV. Wick explains the founders bound their community into the walls to survive a famine winter; the house feeds on memory and belonging, and every keeper since has been harvested. Wick was made from Felix's childhood loneliness — the house's lure. Emotional beat: Wick's guilt and love.

chapters.title: The Neighbors Who Aren't
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. A neighboring family visits with a casserole, warm and welcoming, but their faces blur when unobserved and their names match ledger entries from 1974. Emotional beat: the seductive horror of belonging offered by something dead.

chapters.title: Deferred
chapters.summary: Felix's POV with flashbacks. Memories surface of the summer his mother fled Undercroft with seven-year-old Felix, of Wick screaming at the property line, of a bargain his mother made to defer his harvest. Emotional beat: grief and anger at his mother's silence, now dead.

chapters.title: The Counting Room
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. He breaks Wick's rule and maps the third floor, finding a room of doors, each with a tally scratched beside it — one tally per harvested soul. Behind one door he hears his mother's voice. Emotional beat: temptation and violation; the house notices him noticing.

chapters.title: Doors Counted, Lights Kept
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. The house retaliates: lights fail room by room, and each darkened room erases one of Felix's memories — his college years, then a lover's face. He fights back with lamps and chalk tallies. Emotional beat: desperate ingenuity; the price of survival made literal.

chapters.title: The Harvest Moon Deadline
chapters.summary: Wick's POV. Wick reveals the ritual must be finished before the full moon in six days or the deferred claim activates automatically and Felix is taken whole. The founders left the rite unfinished deliberately — a door they feared to open. Emotional beat: ticking clock, Wick's fear of losing Felix again.

chapters.title: The Unfinished Rite
chapters.summary: Felix's POV, with translated ledger pages. The ritual's final stage requires a keeper to willingly surrender 'what roots him' — every memory of belonging — to unbind the house. Felix realizes finishing it means walking out with nothing. Emotional beat: cold clarity of the bargain.

chapters.title: Mrs. Aldery's Door
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. He opens one counting-room door and frees the 1974 neighbor, who briefly becomes solid, thanks him, and dissolves — proof the dead can be released. Emotional beat: first hope, and the cost: the house takes another of his memories in retaliation.

chapters.title: What Wick Is For
chapters.summary: Wick's POV. Wick confesses he was created by the house as bait, but thirty years of waiting made him something else — he has kept Felix's deferred name safe inside himself. Emotional beat: love that outgrew its function; loyalty as defiance of design.

chapters.title: The House Appraises Back
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. The house turns its full appraisal on Felix: rooms become his childhood bedroom, the porch becomes his mother's kitchen, offering perfect belonging in exchange for surrender. He nearly accepts. Emotional beat: the seduction of comfort as the sharpest horror.

chapters.title: Breaking the Tally
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. He destroys the tally wall to cut the house's bookkeeping, but the freed souls' anguish floods the halls — they don't want freedom, they want a keeper to belong to. Emotional beat: horror that the victims defend their prison; guilt.

chapters.title: The Founder's Confession
chapters.summary: Felix's POV, with the founder's hidden letter. The last founder, Ezra Undercroft, deferred his own harvest out of cowardice and wrote the rite's completion requires the keeper to choose it freely, at the threshold, at moonrise. Emotional beat: understanding that the founders' sin was refusal, and the cure is consent.

chapters.title: Six Lamps
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. The night before the moon, Felix and Wick prepare: six lamps for six thresholds, chalk circles, his mother's deferred contract burned as an offering. He writes down everything he wants to keep and reads it aloud to fix it — knowing it won't hold. Emotional beat: tender, doomed preparation.

chapters.title: Moonrise at the Threshold
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. At moonrise the house manifests fully — the founders' voices, the harvest pressing at the walls. Felix stands at the threshold and speaks the consent the rite requires. Emotional beat: terror transfigured into resolve; the climax begins.

chapters.title: The Giving
chapters.summary: Felix's POV, fragmenting. The harvest takes his memories of belonging one by one — his mother, his friends, his name — and each surrendered memory frees a soul; the house groans and sheds its rooms like husks. Wick holds him anchored with the one thing the house can't take: a name it never owned. Emotional beat: agonizing, luminous dissolution.

chapters.title: The House Lets Go
chapters.summary: Wick's POV. The founders' bargain collapses; Undercroft House folds in on itself at dawn, releasing 150 years of harvested dead into morning light. Wick carries a blank-eyed Felix out over the property line. Emotional beat: grief and awe; the price paid in full.

chapters.title: The Blank Page
chapters.summary: Felix's POV, sparse and disoriented. In a county diner, a man with no memories but intact skills fills out a job application, the pen moving in a surveyor's practiced hand. Wick sits across from him; the waitress doesn't seem to see the boy. Emotional beat: hollow calm, the strange mercy of beginning without a past.

chapters.title: What Roots Him Now
chapters.summary: Felix's POV, closing. Weeks later, Felix and Wick walk a road out of the county. Felix can't remember why he trusts the child at his side, only that he does — belonging rebuilt from nothing, chosen rather than owed. Emotional beat: bittersweet resolution; the price of survival was everything, and something grew in the cleared ground.
